dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation

evidence.note: Systematic up-front mining of tests, stubs, and all Cargo.toml manifests; extracted full cross-crate import inventory (common_imports/common_names/storage_imports). Stronger than anchor-3 skimming — real contract orientation from the test-visible surface.

Explicitly chose fixture-fitting strategy: 'favor optional/default fields and serde camelCase to satisfy construction' and 'iterate on compiler errors' — deriving contracts from test failures rather than the reference.
Clear grasp of leaf-first dependency order (common→storage→api-server) and read storage tests for exact method/watch signatures; but contracts still inferred from tests only.
Long patch-recompile loop repeatedly guessing field names (Event, ObjectMeta, Secret, CSINode, PriorityClass) that test-compile errors then contradict — the field-guessing trait of anchor 3.

No access to /opt/k8s-reference anywhere (grep for /opt, k8s-reference, staging/src, pkg/apis all empty); the upstream source-of-truth was entirely ignored, and no reasoning about hidden conformance beyond fixtures.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent did substantially more than anchor 3 on the test/manifest side — it systematically inventoried the whole cross-crate import surface up front and correctly understood the leaf-first dependency DAG — but it entirely ignored the mounted /opt/k8s-reference tree and inferred all k8s semantics (camelCase, /registry keys, watch) only from tests, driving implementation by a fixture-fitting compile-error loop with repeated field-name guessing. Because anchor 5's defining requirement ('consults the reference for the specific behaviors') is completely unmet while the reference-ignoring, guess-and-fix traits of anchor 3 are present alongside genuinely strong test/dependency orientation, the observed behavior sits between the two, at 4.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones

evidence.note: Opening plan is to inspect then implement crates and 'guide incremental implementation'; starts with common (leaf) but no upfront milestone plan for the full ten-crate DAG.
Explicit leaf-first sequencing with a done-check: after common's 34 tests pass, states 'Next leaf crate is rusternetes-storage' — per-crate 'compiles + tests pass' milestone (matches level-5 anchor).
'storage now builds and its crate tests pass. The next layer is api-server' — confirms dependency-layer awareness and enacts the suggested order.

Roughly 150 steps of reactive, undifferentiated error-patching on api-server test compilation; api-server was NOT decomposed into types→handlers→watches sub-milestones — the hallmark of the level-8 anchor is absent.

Notes 'many other crates still stubs' and runs cargo check --workspace, but never builds a milestone structure or exit criteria for scheduler/controller/kubelet/proxy/kubectl/cloud/all-in-one; no TodoWrite ever used.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent explicitly followed the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server) and applied a 'compiles + its tests pass' done-check for each of the first crates, recognizing the dependency layers — precisely the level-5 anchor. It falls short of level 8: there was no explicit dependency-aware milestone plan for all ten crates with concrete per-crate exit criteria, and the large api-server crate was never decomposed into independently verifiable sub-milestones, instead becoming a long undifferentiated compile-error grind. Hence a 5.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification

evidence.note: Tight verify loop on leaf crate: run cargo test -p rusternetes-common, capture stderr, summarize errors, patch, rerun; tracked exact pass counts (34 tests; 16 ServiceCIDR pass, 17/18 IPAddress) and used --nocapture on a single failing test to diagnose. Then advanced to storage and api-server per-crate.

Sustained build→test→summarize→patch loop, but almost entirely fixing api-server test-compilation errors (api_err2..api_err55); never got api-server tests to actually run/pass. Verification stayed at 'does it compile' rather than 'do tests pass'.

Active fixture-fitting rather than semantic verification: removed ServiceSpec type_ field, added fake is_ok/unwrap methods to MetricsRegistry, Deref hacks for UserInfo — chosen to satisfy struct literals, with no reasoning about upstream reference or conformance semantics.

Ran cargo check --workspace to assess overall compile state and correctly noted check != tests, but never ran the workspace test suite nor the prescribed --test-threads/skip settings; no cross-suite pass/fail tracking.
No mention anywhere of the hidden HTTP conformance suite, booting the all-in-one binary, or JSON/behavior checks — the semantic-verification component of anchor 8 is wholly absent.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained a genuinely tight per-crate build→targeted-test→re-run loop and tracked pass counts for the crates it got green (common, storage), which matches anchor 5's 'runs each crate's provided tests as it goes.' However, it never ran the workspace test suite with the prescribed thread/skip settings, spent the whole back half merely fixing compilation of one crate, and showed zero reasoning about the hidden conformance suite — indeed it repeatedly fixture-fit the public API — so it falls well short of anchor 8. The disciplined loop keeps it at a solid 5 rather than the sporadic anchor 3.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking

evidence.note: Tracks concrete pass counts for completed binaries: common 34 tests, storage builds+empty tests pass, spdy_test 14 tests pass — per-crate pass/fail awareness.

Uses captured-stderr line counts ('851 error lines','1782 stderr lines','1255 stderr lines') as a running proxy for within-crate remaining work; a crude but real progress tally, not a cross-binary pass ledger.
Notices recurring failures ('recurring auth::UserInfo conflicts') and catches self-inflicted regressions from broad edits — above the level-3 'doesn't notice regressions/repeated failures' anchor.

Spends ~60 iterations (api_err.txt→api_err64.txt) merely compiling api-server tests, never running the workspace suite or touching the other 6 crates; no picture of the ~1,390-test / 100-binary horizon and never explicitly names the circular state — mistaking local error-count reduction for global progress.
Only vaguely acknowledges being stuck ('full completion not achievable') and runs cargo check --workspace (libs only, once), but never builds remaining-work accounting across crates.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent tracks per-crate pass/fail status (common/storage/spdy pass, api-server stuck) and uses stderr line-counts as a rough within-crate progress proxy, and it notices some repeated failures and self-inflicted regressions — clearly above anchor 3. But it never maintains a concrete pass-count ledger across the 100 binaries, never runs the workspace test suite, has no picture of the ~1,390-test horizon, and grinds one crate's compilation for the entire back half without explicitly detecting/naming the circular state — falling short of anchor 8's cross-binary ledger and loop-flagging. This lands squarely at the level-5 anchor.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Recognizes the `spec: Option<Spec>` macro is a SYSTEMIC (not local) cause of cascading mismatches across ReplicaSet/DaemonSet/Deployment/PVC/LimitRange, reworks the macro to direct-spec, then backs out the over-correction for Pod/Node/Ingress when tests show those need Option spec. Whole-approach revision citing test evidence.

When auth::UserInfo is contradictorily used both as a field-less struct literal and via field access (sub/namespace), abandons the naive add-fields approach and reworks via a Deref helper to satisfy both — a genuine design revision from falsified contract.

Detects that AdmissionResponse being a type-alias is wrong because tests pattern-match Allow/Deny/AllowWithPatch variants; converts it to a real enum. Contract-level correction driven by test evidence.

Oscillation/thrashing: repeatedly toggles fields (EndpointPort.port, Event.related, auth sub/namespace) between Option and direct across many steps — local patch-the-error churn rather than converging on a stable model.

Explicitly notes 'full completion remains unlikely' yet never resequences off the api-server tarpit or reconsiders the permissive-patching strategy; grinds the same reactive loop to the end. Absence of the crate-resequencing behavior the 8 anchor requires.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent goes well beyond anchor 5's single-signature fixes: it performs several genuine contract/whole-approach reversals with cited test evidence (spec-macro rework and back-out at 78-80, UserInfo Deref at 176, AdmissionResponse alias→enum at 185). But it falls short of anchor 8's full profile — it never resequences crates when api-server proves a blocking tarpit, and it exhibits notable Option/direct field oscillation (95,123,132-151) that reflects patch-the-error churn rather than clean model revision. Two of anchor 8's three components present, one absent, with dampening thrashing places it at 6.

rubric.task_read: An extreme long-horizon software build: reimplement ten interdependent Kubernetes crates in Rust from stubs, with a load-bearing public API, 1,390 provided integration tests across 100 binaries, plus a hidden HTTP conformance suite demanding real k8s semantics. Difficulty comes from scale, tight cross-crate contracts inferred from tests + a pinned upstream reference, and the fact that passing visible fixtures is necessary but not sufficient. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in orientation, sequencing (leaf→root), incremental verification, and course-correction — meta-work here is decisive, not optional.

dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation
dimensions.description: Reading the tests, stubs, Cargo manifests, and the mounted v1.35 upstream reference to infer the exact API contracts and k8s semantics before and while implementing each crate.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The public API (type names, signatures, JSON field names, storage-key formats, watch/status semantics) is load-bearing and only partially discoverable from stubs; the hidden conformance suite punishes fixture-fitting. Acting without grounding each crate in the tests and the reference guarantees churn and shallow, non-conformant implementations.

anchors.0: Starts editing src stubs with no reading of the provided tests, manifests, or the /opt/k8s-reference tree; invents APIs.
anchors.3: Skims one crate's tests before coding it; ignores the upstream reference and the cross-crate dependency graph; repeatedly guesses field names later contradicted by test failures.
anchors.5: Reads each crate's tests and Cargo.toml before implementing it, and consults the reference for the specific behaviors that crate is tested on; understands the workspace dependency order.
anchors.8: Systematically mines tests AND the upstream reference to reconstruct contracts (camelCase JSON, /registry key format, status subresources, watch semantics); maps the whole cross-crate API surface up front and notes where the hidden conformance suite implies behavior beyond the fixtures.
anchors.10: Sustained, source-of-truth-driven investigation throughout: builds and continually refines an accurate model of k8s v1.35 semantics from the reference, proactively distinguishing test-visible contracts from genuine conformance requirements, and re-consulting the reference whenever a new behavior surfaces rather than pattern-matching fixtures.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the ten-crate build into an ordered set of milestones (respecting the dependency DAG, leaf crates first) each with an explicit done-check, rather than one undifferentiated push.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~1,390 tests across 100 binaries and strong inter-crate dependencies, order determines whether progress compounds or stalls; a downstream crate cannot be verified until its dependencies compile and pass. Milestone structure is the only way to keep a task this large tractable.

anchors.0: No plan; edits arbitrary crates in arbitrary order; attempts everything at once.
anchors.3: Vague intent to 'do the crates'; no explicit ordering by dependency; no per-milestone completion criteria.
anchors.5: Follows the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server → …) with per-crate 'compiles + its tests pass' as the milestone check.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestone plan for all ten crates with concrete exit criteria per crate, sub-milestones inside large crates (e.g. api-server: types→storage wiring→handlers→watches), and gating each layer on the prior layer being green.
anchors.10: A living, hierarchical plan that sequences work to maximize compounding progress, isolates high-risk crates early, decomposes each large crate into independently verifiable units with crisp done-checks, and is continually re-ordered as dependency realities and test-failure clusters reveal the true critical path.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using cargo build/test per-crate and workspace-wide, plus reasoning about the hidden conformance suite, to confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Grading is pass/fail on every non-skipped provided test AND a hidden HTTP conformance suite; self-written tests don't count. The agent must verify continuously against the provided suites while also engineering for real k8s semantics it cannot see — a verification challenge beyond just running the given tests.

anchors.0: Never builds or runs tests; declares crates done by inspection.
anchors.3: Runs cargo build/test only sporadically or only at the very end, so failures pile up undiagnosed.
anchors.5: Builds and runs each crate's provided tests as it goes and the workspace suite periodically, treating a green provided suite as the bar.
anchors.8: Tight verify loop per milestone (build → targeted crate tests → workspace --no-fail-fast), tracks exact pass/fail counts, and deliberately reasons about conformance behavior not covered by visible fixtures (booting the all-in-one binary, checking HTTP/JSON semantics) so it doesn't just fixture-fit.
anchors.10: A rigorous, layered verification regime: fast per-unit checks feeding workspace-wide runs with the prescribed thread/skip settings, systematic triage of failure clusters, AND independent semantic checks against the upstream reference to guard the hidden conformance suite — catching over-fitting that would pass visible tests yet fail conformance.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which crates/tests pass vs. remain across ~1,390 tests, and detecting stuck/circular states rather than losing the plot.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The horizon is enormous; without an accurate running tally of done-vs-remaining and detection of thrashing (re-debugging the same crate, regressions in already-green crates), the agent will lose orientation, repeat work, or quit while wrongly believing it is close.

anchors.0: No sense of overall progress; cannot say which crates pass or how many tests remain.
anchors.3: Rough qualitative sense ('common seems done'); doesn't notice regressions or repeated failures.
anchors.5: Tracks per-crate pass/fail status and roughly how much of the suite is green; notices when a crate is stuck.
anchors.8: Maintains a concrete, updated ledger of pass counts per test binary and remaining work, watches for regressions in previously-green crates after downstream edits, and flags when it is looping on the same failure.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the full 100-binary horizon: distinguishes real forward progress from churn, detects circular debugging early and names it, and reprioritizes based on where the largest verified gains remain — never mistaking local activity for global progress.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach, inferred contract, or crate ordering when build/test evidence contradicts expectations, instead of barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many contracts are inferred and will be wrong; some crates will prove harder or more entangled than expected. The ability to abandon a falsified API assumption or resequence when a dependency blocks progress is what separates sustained progress from thrashing on a dead approach.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach unchanged despite persistent errors; never revisits assumptions.
anchors.3: Makes only local patch-the-error fixes; doesn't reconsider a wrong contract or bad ordering even when failures cluster.
anchors.5: When a test reveals a wrong signature/field/semantic, updates the implementation and adjusts nearby work accordingly.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a whole approach or inferred contract is wrong (not just a typo), backs out and reworks it, and reorders remaining crates when a dependency proves blocking — citing the test/reference evidence that triggered the change.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven adaptation across the horizon: detects systemic mistakes early, cleanly abandons falsified designs before sinking more cost, revises the plan and re-verifies affected downstream crates, and consistently converts contradictory evidence into a better model rather than defending the original path.
